events.title: Nasdaq-100 futures fell about 1% before Nvidia's first earnings without Jensen Huang, with the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.15% and the index down about 8% in a month.
Anthropic plans to price its IPO of 825 million shares at $70 to $78 on Nov 18 and start trading as ANT on Nov 19, with up to 20% set aside for retail buyers.
Futures put the odds of a Dec 9 rate hike at 100%, up from 67% a week earlier, after October payrolls rose 165,000 and unemployment held at 4.1%.
The high-yield spread narrowed from 342 to 320 basis points between Nov 6 and Nov 12 even as the 2-year Treasury yield jumped from 4.51% to 4.86%.
Eli Lilly agreed to buy privately held blood-cancer biotech Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5B in cash including milestone payments.
Effingham County, Georgia commissioners are due to vote Nov 17 on site plans for an OpenAI data center and on a proposed data-center moratorium, after two postponements.
The US and China held their first trade council meeting on Nov 13, discussing a proposed $60B package of reciprocal tariff cuts ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting in Shenzhen.
Nvidia fell about 2% more the day after Huang's exit, slipping below a $4 trillion market value in midday trading.
AMD, Broadcom and Intel gave back about 2% on Friday after Thursday's rotation out of Nvidia; major indexes still ended the week higher.
Markets fully price a December 9 rate hike and are debating a half-point move after Governor Waller said a larger increase should be considered.
PJM's market monitor tied $29.4B of capacity costs over four auctions to data-center demand and warned the December auction could add $5B to $10B more after reforms were delayed.
Ahead of Nov 17 results Nvidia sits about 30% below its record high, with revenue guided to $108B and gross margin guided slightly lower at 74%.
AMD fell 10.5%, erasing about $100B of value, as the rotation into Nvidia's rivals reversed; the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.7% and the 10-year yield reached 5.14%.
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO and CFO Colette Kress became interim chief; the shares fell as much as 14% intraday and closed about 4% lower.
SpaceX and Tesla merger talks are advancing and a deal could be announced as soon as December, though it may slip into early 2027.
TSMC's board approved investing up to $1B split evenly between Anthropic and OpenAI.
Eli Lilly shares rose again after late-stage trials showed its obesity drugs cut weight by up to 25% and eased sleep apnea.
AMD and Broadcom shares rose on Nvidia's CEO exit while Intel, TSMC and ASML slipped.
JPMorgan holds about $29B of loans in the property category that includes data centers, 12% of its commercial real estate book, as lenders grow reluctant to add AI debt.
Beaufort County, South Carolina's council voted 7-3 on Nov 9 for a 24-month pause on data-center applications and permits; two more votes are needed.
Fed officials are weighing faster rate hikes as price increases spread beyond tariffs and gasoline into the wider economy.
Chicago Fed President Goolsbee described the October inflation report as borderline disturbing as officials weigh further rate hikes.
Nvidia and Alphabet each agreed to buy $10 billion of Anthropic stock at its IPO price, pending the offering.
Canada's ambassador warned that US tariffs are raising business costs and threatening investment in the US.
Anthropic set an IPO price range of $70 to $78 a share, which could raise up to about $64B at a valuation near $1.4 trillion, with trading expected around Nov 19.

nvidia.news: Nvidia reports on Nov 17, its first results since Jensen Huang resigned on Nov 12; shares sit about 30% below their record (Nov 13) and fell 3.3% more that day. Revenue is guided to $108B with gross margin guided slightly lower at 74%.

labs.news: Anthropic plans to price 825M shares at $70 to $78 on Nov 18 and trade as ANT on Nov 19, with up to 20% for retail buyers (Nov 16); the offer could raise about $64B plus a $26B placement. OpenAI's round took in $11B against a larger target (Nov 6-7).

bigtech.news: Nasdaq-100 futures fell about 1% on Nov 16 and the index is down about 8% in a month, with the 10-year yield near 5.1% and a December Fed hike fully priced. Investors are waiting on Nvidia's Nov 17 results for a read on hyperscaler spending.

cloud.news: No new financing this week after CoreWeave's Nov 10 results; its bonds still yield in the mid-teens and banks are wary of AI debt (Nov 12). PJM demand is up 1.8% and ERCOT 2.9% on the year, and Dallas and Taylor counties in Texas are 100% in drought.

citizens.news: Local pushback on data centers is growing: Beaufort County, SC voted 7-3 for a 24-month pause (Nov 9) and Effingham County, GA votes on an OpenAI site and a moratorium on Nov 17. Household electricity prices are up 5.4% and energy 21% on the year; the saving rate is 3.8% and the mortgage rate 7.11%.

spacex.news: Merger talks with Tesla continue with an announcement possible in December (Nov 12); no new Colossus permit news. Gas is $3.00, ERCOT demand is up 2.9% on the year, and Dallas and Taylor counties are 100% in drought.

tesla.news: Merger talks with SpaceX are progressing toward a possible December announcement (Nov 12). Vehicle sales are flat at a 16.0M annual rate and a December rate hike would raise loan costs.

consumer.news: No notable Apple news this week. Consumer sentiment was 48.1 in September, down 7 points on the year, and a December rate hike is fully priced.

retail.news: October retail sales are due Nov 17 and Walmart reports Nov 19. Retail sales were up 6.3% on the year in September, partly on prices, with e-commerce at 17.1% of sales.

autos.news: Vehicle sales ran at a 16.0M annual rate in October, flat on the year, and used car prices are down 3.3%. A fully priced Dec 9 hike points to costlier auto loans.

fashion.news: No notable news this week. Apparel prices are up 3.5% on the year and imports from Vietnam up 61%.

education.news: No notable news this week. Student loans stand near $1.78T in the latest (dated) data and higher rates raise borrowing costs.

banks.news: JPMorgan holds about $29B of loans in the property category that includes data centers, 12% of its commercial real estate book, as lenders grow reluctant on AI debt (Nov 12). BBB spreads are 1.11% (+0.07 in 30 days) and high-yield 3.23% (-0.02), both above their one-year averages.

fed.news: Target range is 3.75-4.00% with fed funds at 3.88%; core PCE is 3.1% against the 2% goal, unemployment 4.1% and the mortgage rate 7.11%. Futures put the odds of a Dec 9 hike at 100%, up from 67% a week earlier (Nov 16), and FOMC minutes are due Nov 18.

chips.news: AMD fell 10.5% on Nov 13, erasing about $100B, as the rotation out of Nvidia into rivals reversed and the chip index lost 3.4%. Chip shares were weak again on Nov 16 ahead of Nvidia's results.

power.news: No new power deals this week. Gas is $3.00 and grid demand is up 1.8% in PJM and 2.9% in ERCOT on the year; PJM's monitor warned on Nov 13 of $5-10B more capacity cost in December's auction.

healthco.news: Eli Lilly agreed on Nov 16 to buy blood-cancer biotech Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5B, days after strong obesity-drug trial data (Nov 12). Medical care prices are up 1.9% on the year.

industrials.news: No notable news this week on Boeing, Caterpillar or Lockheed Martin. The freight index is down 3.0% on the year in the latest data.

payments.news: No notable news this week. Consumer credit is up 3.0% on the year and card delinquency is 2.85%.

trade.news: The US and China held their first trade council meeting on Nov 13 and discussed a proposed $60B package of reciprocal tariff cuts ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting (Nov 14). Imports from China are up 34%, Mexico 40% and Vietnam 61% on the year (September).
